title: Mileage Allowance for Kestrel Advantage Balloon Vehicles Returned Before or After Maturity
content:
**Return option terms — mileage allowance basis.** For the excess mileage charge on a returned Kestrel Advantage Balloon Retail Installment Sale Contract, the mileage allowance depends on when the vehicle came back compared with the maturity date. The full-term allowance is the annual mileage allowance times the term in months divided by 12.

| Return date | Mileage allowance |
|---|---|
| Before the maturity date | The full-term allowance prorated by the calendar days from the contract date to the return date over the calendar days from the contract date to the maturity date, rounded to a whole mile |
| After the maturity date, on a contract with installments deferred by extension (installments deferred over the life of the contract above zero) | The annual mileage allowance times the sum of the term in months and the installments deferred, divided by 12, rounded to a whole mile |
| On the maturity date, or after it with no installment ever deferred | The full-term allowance |

Calendar days from one date to another count the later date and not the earlier one. In the proration the full-term allowance is not rounded first; the single rounding to a whole mile comes after the proration.

## Hypothetical cases (annual allowance 12,000 miles, 36-month term)

- **Early return.** 1,000 calendar days from contract date to return date and 1,096 to the maturity date: 36,000 times 1,000 over 1,096 is 32,846.7, rounded to 32,847 miles.
- **Late return with 2 installments deferred.** 12,000 times 38 divided by 12 is 38,000 miles.
- **Late return with nothing deferred.** 36,000 miles.
- **Return on the maturity date.** 36,000 miles.
